newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Wing of Cambodia party rejects alliance.
newsitem.headline: Wing of Cambodia party rejects alliance.

text.p: A further split in Cambodia's fractious political scene was sealed when a wing of the country's third largest party rejected joining an alliance planned by First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.

A statement received on Tuesday said the wing of the BLDP (Buddhist Liberal Democratic Party) led by Information Minister Ieng Mouly "does not have any desire to join the so called 'FUN' (United National Front)" proposed by Ranariddh.
Political analysts expected the move as the wing headed by Ieng Mouly's bitter rival, BLDP founder Son Sann, had already agreed in principle to join the alliance.
Ieng Mouly's move confirmed the split in the BLDP after hopes of a rapprochement ahead of 1998 elections.

The analysts predicted Ieng Mouly would eventually throw in his lot with the Cambodian People's Party (CPP) of Co-Premier Hun Sen, who has also rejected joining the alliance mooted by Ranariddh, his main rival in the strained coalition government.

Ranariddh has said the opposition Khmer Nation Party (KNP), defectors from the Khmer Rouge rebel movement and two smaller groups were ready to join his royalist FUNCINPEC party in the United National Front.
The prince has denied the new alliance is aimed against Hun Sen's CPP, which formed an uneasy coalition with FUNCINPEC after 1993 elections.
Analysts believe Hun Sen's formerly communist CPP could form its own alliance, including Ieng Mouly's BLDP wing and other Khmer Rouge defectors, to fight the royalists' front at the next polls.

The Khmer Rouge, whose brutal rule from 1975-79 left more than one million people dead, boycotted the last elections and fought the coalition, but the movement has unravelled since last August with thousands of guerrillas defecting.
The BLDP contested the elections and won 10 seats in the 120-seat national assembly (parliament).

Their party, as the Khmer People's National Liberation Front, fought alongside the royalists and the Maoist Khmer Rouge against the Vietnam-backed CPP government before signing a peace accord in 1991.
The two leaders later fell out and split in 1995.
